questions.prompt: What money is used in Kosovo?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Kosovo is the euro.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Pristina?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Kosovo is Pristina.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Kosovo?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Subdivisions” part of the Kosovo article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Kosovo?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Kosovo on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Kosovo article.

questions.proof: Kosovo shares borders with Serbia to the north and east, North Macedonia to the southeast, Albania to the southwest, and Montenegro to the west.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Kosovo on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Kosovo on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
